name: ClinuxFlowPatientGraph
description: The real reference-structure graph rooted on Patient — deliberately separate from ClinuxFlowOnboardingGraph.json (that graph's own header correctly excludes Patient: facility-registration topology is a different root/scope from patient-clinical topology, and conflating the two would misrepresent both). ClinuxFlowPatient.json is a genuine leaf profile — zero Reference-typed elements of its own — so there is nothing INTERNAL to Patient for a graph to walk. The one real structural edge Patient has in this system is the reverse one: a facility's Encounters point back to a Patient (real FHIR Encounter.subject). That edge is honestly GraphDefinition-shaped (reference cardinality, not time/sequence) — same reasoning ClinuxFlowOnboardingGraph's own reverse links (role-at-facility, affiliation-from-facility) already establish. Deliberately does NOT model anything INSIDE an Encounter (Register->Triage->Consult->SOAP->Checkout) — that sequence is genuinely episodic/pipeline-shaped (SPEC-16 SS3, SPEC-23 SS4/SS10), which real FHIR GraphDefinition cannot express (no concept of time/state/before-after; see SPEC-24 SS3's own honest split) and which this pass does not build a state machine for either — left as explicitly future, separate work. Walked by the same next-best-action.js as ClinuxFlowOnboardingGraph (no code changes needed): once a Patient resource is valid, this graph's one reverse link surfaces exactly one open-ended, repeatable candidate — 'capture an Encounter for this patient' — which is genuinely useful (it's literally 'what to do next after registering a patient'), not a hollow gesture.

link.description: Every visit/encounter recorded for this patient
